significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that attributed belief and factual truth occupy "geometrically distinct" and "independent[ly] steerab[le]" representations, while truth-direction leakage predicts attribution errors; this combines a form-(ii) causal decomposition with a limited form-(iii) predictive coupling. It would establish both a phenomenon—errors "coincide with the truth direction leaking into the belief readout"—and a mechanism that fixes expectations about which conflict cases should fail and whether belief reports can be changed while factual answers remain stable; this is consequential given that latent-truth work such as Burns et al., "Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision" (ICLR 2023), relies on interpreting internal truth-related structure. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure would rule out the proposed single low-dimensional, independently causal belief channel or its leakage account, although rejection of the conjunctive claim would not by itself identify which component failed. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on LLM beliefs would not warrant this score; the specific two-channel causal decomposition and error coupling, which are false of the median probe-only hypothesis, support the above-median rating.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "lightweight monitor for detecting when a model is about to conflate what an agent believes with what is true," using truth leakage into the belief readout as its measurable warning signal. This is ex ante because "about to conflate" places the activation reading before the downstream report, leaving an auditing or gating window rather than merely explaining an error afterward. Although each model may require re-extracting its directions, the claimed coupling between leakage and later attribution error predicts what recalibration should recover; however, the hypothesis supplies no cross-model invariant threshold, and its own limitations concede that findings "may be model-specific and not transfer across scales/families." Downstream users could include model auditors rather than only belief researchers, and the topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the concrete pre-output monitor and transferable leakage relation—not the broad importance of LLM beliefs—earn the reach rating.
